cohort: Pregnant women in Guatemala, India, Kenya, Pakistan, Zambia, and the Democratic Republic of Congo, including both home and facility births, from 2010 to 2015.
finding: While cesarean section rates increased across all study sites, the procedure was associated with reduced postpartum hemorrhage and stillbirths in non-African sites but an increase in adverse outcomes in African sites.
country: Guatemala, India, Kenya, Pakistan, Zambia, and Democratic Republic of Congo
